dashboard-view.intro: The page you open first every day: announcements, punch buttons, your personal profile, and any attendance exceptions the system found.
steps: Tap "Punch In" when you arrive and "Punch Out" before you leave; both the time and your GPS location are recorded.
If your phone supports fingerprint or face recognition, tap "Set up biometrics" once to pair it, then punch with biometrics from then on.
If you forgot to punch or the time is wrong, submit a make-up punch request with a reason and wait for the administrator's approval.
Fill in your ID number, address, phone and birthday under "My profile" - payroll and insurance work needs them.
notes: Punching requires location permission; if the browser blocks it, the punch fails or is recorded as an exception.
"Attendance exceptions" are detected automatically (missing punch, late, early leave). An approved make-up punch clears the exception.
Announcements are sorted by importance; red ones are important, please read them.
terms: Biometric punch
Pairs this phone with your account so fingerprint or face recognition replaces the punch button. Location is still recorded.
Make-up punch
A punch entered after the fact; it only enters the attendance record once an administrator approves it.

monthly-view.intro: See your whole month on a calendar: which days were normal, which had exceptions, and how much overtime you worked.
steps: The four figures on top are this month's statistics; the calendar below colors each day by status.
Use "<" and ">" to change month; tap a day to list all punch records for that day.
If a day's record is wrong, submit a make-up punch request right from that day's card.
notes: Statistics are calculated live: refresh after a make-up punch or leave request is approved and the numbers update.
You only see your own records; supervisors and administrators see company-wide data.
terms: Exception days
Days flagged for a missing punch-in or punch-out, lateness, early leave and so on.
Normal days
Days with both punches recorded at times that match your shift.

location-view.intro: Check the location your phone is currently reporting - useful before punching if you are unsure the position is accurate.
steps: Allow the browser to read your location; the map marks your current coordinates.
Compare "Status" and "Coordinates" to confirm you are inside the office or work site area.
If the position is clearly off, move near a window or outdoors, turn on GPS, and refresh.
notes: Indoors or on Wi-Fi only, the error can reach several hundred meters - that is normal.
If a punch is rejected as out of range, check this page first, then report it to the administrator.

shift-view.intro: See your shift for today and the days ahead; editing shifts happens in shift management.
steps: "Today's shift" shows today's shift type, working hours and location.
To add, adjust or batch-assign shifts, tap "Enter shift management" for the full page.
notes: Regular employees can only view their own shifts; changes are made by administrators.
Shifts drive the late/early-leave rules, so report a wrong shift as soon as you spot it.

overtime-view.intro: Apply for overtime and track approval; approved hours feed into payroll.
steps: Pick the overtime date and enter start and end times - the hours are calculated for you.
Explain the reason in the reason field (the more specific the better) and submit.
Check each request's status - pending, approved or rejected - under "Overtime records".
notes: Apply in advance or the same day where possible; requests filed long after the fact may be rejected.
Approved overtime cannot be edited or deleted by you - ask an administrator for corrections.
Hours are converted into overtime pay or compensatory leave using the statutory rates.
terms: Overtime hours
End time minus start time, with no break deducted - subtract your break yourself before entering.
Compensatory leave
Overtime hours converted into leave hours, used later as "Compensatory leave" on the leave page.

leave-view.intro: Check your remaining hours per leave type, submit leave requests, and track their progress.
steps: Look at "Leave balance" first to confirm how many hours of that type are left.
Choose the leave type, dates and times - the hours are calculated - then write the reason.
Track the status under "Leave records"; a request still pending can be cancelled and resubmitted.
notes: Annual and compensatory leave are capped by your balance; requests above the balance cannot be submitted.
Sick, bereavement and marriage leave may require supporting documents under company policy.
If you are already scheduled during the leave, confirm cover with your supervisor after approval.
terms: Annual leave
Yearly paid leave granted by length of service; unused days are handled per company policy.
Compensatory leave
Leave earned from approved overtime hours, available until used up.

salary-view.intro: The entry point for payroll; the actual payslips, settings and calculations live in the payroll system.
steps: Tap "Enter payroll system" to open the full payroll page.
Employees can view their own payslips; administrators additionally see settings and calculation tools.
notes: Payroll data is confidential - avoid leaving this page open in public or on shared devices.
If an amount looks wrong, compare it with your attendance and overtime records before contacting the administrator.

worklog-view.intro: Record a daily work log: what you did and how many hours it took.
steps: Pick the date and enter the hours worked (decimals allowed, e.g. 8.5).
Describe the day's work in at least 10 characters - be specific.
After submitting, review past logs and their approval status in the records section below.
notes: One log per day as a rule; a duplicate entry will overwrite the first or be returned.
Logged hours are entered by you and tracked separately from punch hours; the two need not match.

admin-view.intro: Administrators only: announcements, approvals, punch locations, attendance analysis and report exports all live here.
steps: Publish announcements under "Announcement management"; set priority to "Important" so staff see it first.
Handle make-up punch and virtual card requests under "Pending requests"; overtime, leave and work logs have their own approval sections.
Add or adjust the allowed punch coordinates and radius under "Punch locations" - this directly decides whether staff can punch.
"Attendance analysis" shows overall hours and punch-time distribution; the report section exports Excel for HR or accounting.
notes: Approvals affect attendance and payroll immediately; when rejecting, state the reason so the employee knows how to fix it.
Too small a radius blocks legitimate punches; too large defeats the purpose of location control.
Exported files contain personal and salary data - do not forward them outside the company.
terms: Virtual card
An alternative punch method approved by an administrator when location punching is unavailable.
Punch radius
The distance in meters around the configured coordinates within which punching is allowed.

view-tab.intro: Review the shifts assigned over a chosen period and confirm who works which shift each day.
steps: Pick a month or date range and search; the table lists every shift in that period.
To change one shift, edit that row directly, or delete it and add it again.
notes: Shift changes affect late/early-leave rules and payroll, so finish adjustments before the shift day.

add-tab.intro: Add a single shift: employee, date, shift type and location.
steps: Pick the employee and date, then the shift type - the hours fill in automatically.
Confirm the work location and submit, then check "View shifts" to see it listed.
notes: Two shifts for the same person on the same day conflict - check the day before adding.

batch-tab.intro: Assign shifts for several employees over a whole period at once - ideal for next month's regular roster.
steps: Choose the date range and the shift type, then tick the employees to schedule.
Set which weekdays to schedule (for example Monday to Friday) and submit.
Afterwards spot-check a few days under "View shifts" to confirm the result.
notes: Batch scheduling creates a lot of records - double-check the range and the people before submitting.
Public holidays and approved leave are not skipped automatically; review and adjust them yourself.

stats-tab.intro: Statistics for the roster: how many days each person is scheduled and whether shift types are evenly spread.
steps: Pick the period and search; the chart and table update together.
If someone has clearly too many or too few shifts, go back to batch scheduling to rebalance.
notes: Only scheduled shifts are counted, not actual attendance - see the attendance records for that.

employee-salary.intro: Employees view their own payslip: base pay, allowances, overtime pay and deductions.
steps: Pick the year and month to list that month's payslip details.
If an amount looks wrong, compare it with the same month's attendance and overtime records before contacting the administrator.
notes: Salary data is confidential - avoid opening or screenshotting it on shared devices.

salary-setting.intro: Administrators set each employee's pay terms: monthly or hourly, allowances, and labor/health insurance brackets.
steps: Pick the employee, set the pay type (monthly or hourly) and the base amount.
Enter meal and attendance allowances plus the insurance and pension brackets, then save.
notes: Settings apply to later payroll runs - confirm the effective month before changing them.
Use the officially published bracket tables; a wrong bracket produces wrong deductions.
terms: Monthly pay
A fixed monthly salary; leave and absences are deducted pro rata from the daily rate.
Hourly pay
Pay based on actual hours worked, taken from the punch records.

monthly-calc.intro: Calculate this month's pay for monthly-paid staff: attendance, overtime and leave produce the gross amount.
steps: Pick the month and employee, run the calculation and review the result.
Confirm the attendance days, overtime hours and deductions, then save it as an official payslip.
notes: Approve all make-up punches, overtime and leave for the month first, or the result will be short.
Recalculating the same month overwrites the previous result.

hourly-calc.intro: Calculate this month's pay for hourly staff; the hours come straight from the punch records.
steps: Pick the month and employee - total attendance and overtime hours are filled in for you.
Verify the hours, then calculate and save.
notes: Missing punches make the hours too low - clear all make-up punch requests before calculating.

salary-list.intro: Look up the payslips already generated, as the basis for payment and reconciliation.
steps: Pick a year and month; the list shows each employee's gross pay, deductions and net pay.
Export the report from here for reconciliation or for accounting.
notes: Do not delete a payslip that has already been paid - make an adjustment entry instead and keep the record.

bonus-records.intro: Records of the three-festival bonuses: how much was paid for Dragon Boat, Mid-Autumn and Lunar New Year.
steps: Pick a year to see that year's bonus records.
Administrators can add or adjust amounts; employees only see their own.
notes: Festival bonuses are not part of regular salary calculation but are still income and appear in annual income data.
